fix.summary:
R1 confirmed and fixed at its cause in /home/y-guo/reproduce/new1/run.py (`_close_failed_launches`, the only file touched).

Verification before the fix, with a script against a temporary ledger (/tmp/claude-12114/-home-y-guo-reproduce-new1/54da0555-0a40-4cf8-b8c1-72bfb652a6f7/scratchpad/verify_r1.py, `registry._repo_root` pointed at a temp tree so the real jobs/runs.jsonl was never written):
  A relaunch in the gap: finish rows=[('launch_failed', 17.9)] open=[]
  B two overlapping ls: finish rows=[('launch_failed', 7217.9), ('launch_failed', 0.0)] open=[]
  C the plain stale launch: finish rows=[('launch_failed', 7217.9)] open=[]
Section A reproduces the reviewer's shape exactly: the relaunch's live launch is closed for good, with `elapsed_s` measured from the relaunch's own start row. Section B reproduces the duplicate row from two overlapping `run.py ls` processes; the second one's `elapsed_s` is 0.0, because `_elapsed` finds no open row by then.

The cause: the writer decided from the row `registry.ls` built and appended inside `registry.lock()` without re-reading which start row is open. The fix states the ownership positively — the row closes the one launch its verdicts describe, and a launch is named by its start row — so under the hold it takes the run's open start row again and appends only while that row is still the judged one (same `run_id`, same `t`), then measures `elapsed_s` from that row rather than from whatever `_elapsed` finds:

    with registry.lock():
        judged = next((r for r in registry.open_runs()
                       if r["run_id"] == run_id and r.get("t") == row.get("t")), None)
        if judged is not None:
            registry.append_finish(run_id, {... "elapsed_s": time.time() - _parse_t(judged["t"])})
            row["status"] = "launch_failed"

`t` is a sound identity here: `launch_failed()` fires only on a start row older than `DEFAULTS["launch_timeout_s"]` (1800 s), so a relaunch's row stands at least half an hour away from the judged one and the minute resolution of `t` cannot collide. The docstring above the function now carries the gap and the two writers that land in it.

Same script after the fix:
  A relaunch in the gap: finish rows=[] open=['train-ccc']
  B two overlapping ls: finish rows=[('launch_failed', 7252.2)] open=[]
  C the plain stale launch: finish rows=[('launch_failed', 7252.2)] open=[]

No VERSION exists in run.py, jobs/launch.py or jobs/registry.py, so no bump applies. jobs/launch.py and jobs/registry.py needed no change: the cause sits entirely in run.py's writer. `_elapsed` stays, `cmd_kill` still calls it.

minors.title: The endpoint clear can delete the document of a server that is still running and still serving another run
minors.detail: jobs/launch.py:476 unlinks `run_dir / p["endpoint_file"]` for every placed service piece before the first `_start_wave`. A relaunch can reach that line while this run's own service session is still alive: the launch gate counts only pieces whose kind is not service (jobs/launch.py:234) and the walk's live-piece test looks at loop and train pieces only (run.py:2032), so a sample or inject run whose loop pieces are dead relaunches with its agent service still up. `_start_wave` then fails on the duplicate session name -- its own docstring states this at jobs/launch.py:388-392 -- and the launch ends through `failed()` -> `teardown_launch` (jobs/launch.py:678) -> `teardown_services`, which returns an empty list without killing anything when `registry._attached_elsewhere(run_id)` is true (jobs/launch.py:652-653, jobs/registry.py:1028-1039), i.e. exactly when another open run is attached to this server. The server therefore keeps running with no `service_agent_<replica>.json` on disk. `_find_attach_target` discovers a target by globbing that file in each open run's directory (jobs/launch.py:791), so the next sample or inject run can no longer see the live server: it loads a second vLLM on the serving host, or exits through `_no_cards_message` because the first one holds the cards. The verdict for M3 dismissed this path on the grounds that `teardown_services` ends the session anyway; that reasoning does not cover the attached-elsewhere skip, which is the ordinary two-runs-one-server case the skip exists for (M-J7). The root statement is that the origin step runs over the pieces this launch starts: a piece whose session name is already taken is not one of them, so the launch should end on that before `incarnation_origin` clears anything, rather than clearing first and discovering the taken name in the next call.

minors.title: `run.py ls`'s one-line help still describes it as printing only, now that it writes finish rows

After this branch, `run.py ls` appends a `launch_failed` finish row to jobs/runs.jsonl and re-renders jobs/RESULTS.md through `registry.append_finish` (run.py:639-643, jobs/registry.py:173-177), which I confirmed against a temporary ledger: one `_close_failed_launches` call on a stale row leaves a finish row and a RESULTS.md whose status column reads `launch_failed`. The `--help` output is the only place an operator or an agent reads what a subcommand does, and both this repo's own review prompts and the gpu-run skill treat `run.py ls` as a read. The help line should name the write, as its two neighbours do.

fix.head: a379e2b
fix.summary:
The one reviewer finding, EVAL-BEAT-1-ERRATA, is correct and I did not fix it: its cause is a stale sentence in `.scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md:155` (and the same sentence in `.scratch/from-zero/issues/08-eval-library-and-classifier-metric.md:407-411`), both outside the two files I may edit. While verifying the branch I did find and fix a real hole in the new pass count, at its cause, inside my file. `report_passes` counted three passes per entry of `cfg.eval.risk`, while `report_classifier` runs those passes over `chosen`, a map keyed by `str(risk)`. first.head: aca7273da0972baf9d9ef4afda70dc1606c49226
first.summary:
EVAL-BEAT-1 fixed in /home/y-guo/reproduce/new1/eval/utils/probe_eval.py. Confirmed the defect in the worktree: `run()` emitted `hb.emit(0, total_events, "item")` at :576 and the next line written was `hb.finish()` at :668, with the whole workload in one `report(...)` call at :617, so `done` never left 0.

WHAT THE FIX DOES. New `report_passes(method, cfg)` returns the number of passes the method's report makes over the prediction frame: `len(cfg.eval.theta_grid) + 3 * len(cfg.eval.risk)` for a classifier (one crossing per theta on val, then per risk target the frozen crossing, its bootstrap and the fires crossing) and `2 * len(cfg.eval.risk)` for a generator (per risk target the join with its row scoring, then its bootstrap). `run()` emits that number as `total` right after the frame is read, and `report`, `report_classifier` and `report_generator` take the heartbeat as their last argument and beat as each pass closes. A risk target whose theta is None closes its passes without doing their work (`beats += 2` in the classifier's frozen loop and the generator's risk loop, `beats += 1` in the fires loop), so `done` reaches `total` for every setting. `total_events` stays exactly where it was, in `done.json`'s `counts["events"]`.

WHY `total` MOVED OFF THE EVENT COUNT. A `done` counted in events is unreachable: both shapes walk the whole frame once per theta and once or more per risk target rather than once per event, and the generator only ever touches the test rows while `total_events` counts every split. The verified `corrected_fix` reaches the same conclusion and asks for an errata entry recording the new total — see concerns, I may not edit that file.

DEVIATION FROM THE CORRECTED FIX. It counts one beat per loop iteration (classifier 20 + 2 + 2 = 24, generator 2 with the default risk list). I split each risk target into the passes it actually makes (classifier 26, generator 4), because `typical_gap_s` needs `min_intervals` = 3 gaps: with 2 beats a generator eval has 2 gaps, `typical_gap_s` still returns None and `stall_line_s` still falls back to `warmup_s` = 1800 s, so consequence (b) would stay unfixed for exactly the shape that carries the per-row `env.split_args` loop. With 4 beats plus the opening one there are 4 gaps.

NO VERSION BUMP. probe_report.json, fires.parquet, consumed.json, report.md and done.json are unchanged; the CPU exercise compares fields and fires frame against the pre-fix module and they are identical in all four cases.

SCORE_RUN.PY: NOT THE SAME DEFECT, NOT CHANGED. eval/score_run.py:201-209 opens with `hb.emit(0, len(pairs), "task")` and emits `hb.emit(i, len(pairs), "task")` inside the record-reading loop, so `done` reaches `total`; `run.py ls --debug` prints `progress=3/3 task rate=24/s` for the four score runs on disk, against `progress=0/16 item rate=0/s` for the five eval runs. It has a different, smaller weakness I did not fix because it is a different defect and out of the ticket: its beats stop when the reading loop ends, while `_spec_block` (a per-row `env.split_args` loop over every spec row, score_run.py:116-130) and `_render_report_md` still run. Since `done == total` by then, `jobs/registry.judge`'s first disjunct calls the piece "done" while the process is still computing. The fourth shape, kept unchanged at lines 116-121, is a launch that did start its pieces ("the service pieces are already up") and did not come up, and it exits 1: `jobs/launch.py:_wait_for_endpoint` (135a6b2, jobs/launch.py:859-868) ends in `sys.exit(f"jobs/launch.py: {path} did not appear within launch_timeout_s")`, which propagates out of `launch.launch` before run.py:2047-2049 can print the `launch returned` line and before any `launch_failed` row is appended. So the paragraph asserts a rule and then names a case that breaks it. The base text had no universal claim (it said "A piece that starts and then fails its alive check is the quiet shape: the call prints nothing at all, exits 0 ..."), so this is introduced by the fix. The narrowing the sentence needs is the outcome, not the pieces: the rule holds for every launch that returns a non-`up` outcome from `launch.launch` (`alive_check`, `service_check`), and the fourth shape exits without returning one.

minors.title: "ending every session this launch started - service, loop and train pieces alike" is unconditional, but teardown_services ends nothing when another live run is attached to this run's service
minors.detail: SKILL.md:107-108 at 135a6b2 states the teardown without exception. `teardown_launch` (jobs/launch.py:653-674) calls `teardown_services` first, and `teardown_services` (jobs/launch.py:630-651) returns `[]` without killing anything when `_attached_elsewhere(run_id)` is true, i.e. when another open run's `service_*.json` names this run_id in `attached_to`; only the non-service pieces are then killed. The code's own docstring carries the caveat ("the `service` pieces through `teardown_services`, which keeps its own `attached_to` skip rule (2.3)"), and the same skill states the rule elsewhere for `kill` (Phase 6b, SKILL.md:198-200: "refuses while another live run is attached to this run's service"). The operator-visible consequence is the one D2 was written to prevent: after a failed launch of a run whose service another live run is attached to, the service pieces are still up and still holding their cards, while the skill says every session this launch started was ended. The printed `ended [...]` list is the only signal that they were not. Note the wording came from the verdict's corrected_fix, so this is a defect inherited from the prescription rather than invented by the fixer.

minors.title: After the revert, job-monitor's autopsy condition and gpu-run's "What is gone" bullet again state something `run.py ls` does not do at this head
minors.detail: 135a6b2 restores job-monitor.md:56-57 ("If `verdict` is `dead`, or an escalating `suspected stall` (`escalated=true`)"), its checklist at :68, and gpu-run/SKILL.md:279-280 ("`ls`'s `escalated` flag survives as something a person reads"). Read at this head, `jobs/registry.py:879` computes `escalated` through `judge`/`judge_service` and `:900` stores it on every piece row, while `run.py:568-579` (`_format_piece`) builds `<index>:<verdict>[@<host>:<session>][ cards=<gpus>]` and never reads `escalated`; nothing else prints it. So D6's consequence is unchanged on this branch: the escalation branch of hard rule 3 tests a value the agent's only permitted source never shows, and an escalating stall is reported without a log tail. This is deliberate and declared - the commit message drops D6 from the branch's claims and the appended errata entry (contract-errata.md, last entry) records the `_format_piece` change as owed and unmade - but the branch is the commit that put the false sentences back (487fba9 had removed them), so the tree at 135a6b2 carries two agent-facing statements the code does not bear out. Nothing closes this except the owed run.py change; flagging so the owner sees it is still open rather than fixed.

minors.title: job-monitor hard rule 3 spells the new `run.py where` command without the probe interpreter, while the same file and gpu-runner spell it with it
minors.detail: The branch adds the same command in three places and spells it two ways. job-monitor.md:27-29 has "`<run_dir>` comes from `external/probe-env/bin/python run.py where <workflow> <setting> <stage>`" and gpu-runner.md:99-100 has the same full spelling, but job-monitor.md:58-59, inside hard rule 3, has "with `<run_dir>` from `run.py where <workflow> <setting> <stage>`" with no interpreter. Hard rule 3 is the one place that sends the agent to a log, so it is the spelling a sonnet agent is most likely to run verbatim; the bare form fails, since the file itself states two paragraphs earlier that this machine has only `python3` and errata entry "0.1 (the interpreter in an acceptance command)" requires the interpreter to be named. Same class as D4/F2, which this branch fixed elsewhere.
